prompt: Why is the proxy's MetaCache keyed by collection ID, with collection names and aliases kept only as hints? And how are cache fills kept from racing the invalidations that DDL broadcasts send, so that a describe started before a DDL can't put stale metadata back?
key: Written in docs/design-docs/design_docs/20260716-proxy-metacache-id-inverted-index.md (dated 2026-07-16; the code now lives in internal/proxy/metacache/meta_cache.go). The primary store used to be keyed by (db, name) while invalidations arrive by id, alias or db, so every id- or alias-driven invalidation did a linear scan under the global write lock; at a large cached working set (target 1M collections) each Load/Release/Drop/Rename/Alter broadcast stalled every query on the proxy for a full-cache sweep. Now the primary store is keyed by the cluster-unique collection id and is the single source of truth; names, aliases and partition lists are hints that resolve to an id and are validated against the primary on every read, so a failed validation is a cache miss (one extra describe), never a stale read. Hints are written only together with their entry and removed with it by one eviction routine (evictCollectionEntryLocked), so nothing dangles and there is no background reclamation; invalidations are O(1), with drop database the one deliberate per-database walk. Fills are ordered against invalidations pessimistically rather than by timestamps: a global fillMu RWMutex, fills (describe RPC + write-back) holding the read side for their whole duration and invalidations taking the write side, draining in-flight fills before evicting, so a pre-DDL snapshot always lands before the eviction that cleans it. This replaced the per-collection timestamp floor (collectionCacheVersion), which had known gaps, and the VersionCache type.
